claims.text: Adding 1.5 at.% Si or 2.0 at.% Cu to an Mg-transition-metal matrix will introduce a transient liquid phase.
The additive-enabled transient liquid phase will permit rapid densification at 850 °C.
Sintering above 900 °C typically causes brittle intermetallic networks and elemental segregation in the proposed Mg-transition-metal system.
The proposed treatment will yield a dense, pseudo-single-phase microstructure with enhanced oxidation resistance.
Sintering additive-free Mg-Mn or Mg-Zr powders over 800-1000 °C results in porous, multiphase structures containing segregated transition-metal clusters.
An Mg-Si or Mg-Cu eutectic reaction will form a transient liquid phase under the proposed 850 °C sintering condition.
The transient liquid will facilitate particle rearrangement and solution-precipitation kinetics.
The transient liquid will dissolve and homogenize Mn or Zr before solidifying into a fine, continuous matrix.
The transient liquid phase lowers the activation energy for diffusion.
Mg volatility becomes significant above 900 °C.
Solid-state diffusion at elevated temperature produces coarse, unstable intermetallic precipitates.
A uniform transition-metal distribution will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The proposed 850 °C treatment will produce relative density exceeding 98%.
The proposed treatment will reduce corrosion current density by at least 50% relative to the baseline.
Standard solid-state sintering at 900-950 °C typically yields relative density below 92% because diffusion is limited.
Standard solid-state sintering at 900-950 °C causes significant Mg loss and coarse, discontinuous intermetallic networks that initiate corrosion.
Below 820 °C, porosity exceeds 5% because insufficient liquid forms.
Above 920 °C, Mg mass loss exceeds 2% because volatility dominates.
Holding at 850 °C for more than 60 minutes causes Mg loss above 2%, surface cracking, and microstructural degradation.
An uncontrolled cooling rate could permit excessive grain growth that negates barrier-property benefits.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that Mg volatility becomes significant above 900 °C, whereas the quantitative boundary says volatility dominates only above 920 °C. These may describe different severity levels, but that distinction is not defined.

The intervention specifies a slight argon overpressure to suppress Mg vaporization, while the conditions allow either 1-2 MPa hot pressing or standard-pressure spark-plasma sintering. Thus, overpressure is presented as required in one field but optional in another.
